title: A torsion normal generator cuts every corona model down to a uniformly full active core

**ESTABLISHED.**  Let `G` be generated by a finite symmetric set `S`, let
`a in S` have finite order `m>=2`, and choose for every `s in S` an
expression as a product of conjugates of `a` or `a^(-1)`.  Let `L` be the
total number of conjugate occurrences in this finite family of expressions.
Let

```text
rho:G -> U(Q_d)
```

be a norm-matrix-corona homomorphism with `rho(a)!=1`.  Then there are
positive integers `k_n`, an operator-norm asymptotic representation

```text
sigma_n:G -> U(k_n),
```

and unitaries `A_n=sigma_n(a)` satisfying `A_n^m=1` such that, after
restricting to an infinite coordinate subsequence on which the mark survives:

1. after coordinate unitary conjugacy, the restricted corona map is represented by
   `sigma_n directSum 1_(d_n-k_n)`;
2. if `p_n=1_(C\{1})(A_n)` and `r_n=rank(p_n)`, then
   ```text
   r_n <= k_n <= L r_n;
   ```
3. consequently
   ```text
   tr_(k_n)(p_n)>=1/L
   ```
   and, with
   `eta_m=min{|1-zeta|:zeta^m=1,zeta!=1}>0`,
   ```text
   ||sigma_n(a)-1||_(2,tr_(k_n))>=eta_m/sqrt(L).
   ```

Thus every nonzero corona image of the torsion mark has a stably equivalent
matrix-corona model in which its active spectral projection is full with a
dimension-independent fullness constant.

The resulting rank scale is intrinsic to the finite-order normal-equivalence
class: `finite-order-normal-generation-controls-corona-rank-scale` shows that
replacing the mark by any finite-order element with the same normal closure
changes its coordinate ranks by at most fixed multiplicative constants.

There is also a quantitative propagation statement.  If a fixed
`g in G` satisfies

```text
a = product of N_g conjugates of g^(+1) or g^(-1),
```

then

```text
liminf_n ||sigma_n(g)-1||_2
  >= eta_m/(N_g sqrt(L)).
```

In particular, if `a` belongs to the normal closure of every nonidentity
element of `G`—for example, if `G` is simple—then every nontrivial corona
homomorphism reblocks to a faithful hyperlinear embedding.  If the normal
generation lengths `N_g` are uniformly bounded, the resulting embedding has
a uniform Hilbert--Schmidt separation constant on `G\{1}`.
